QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_30

question.text: If a Cat III AIF scheme FAILS to obtain 75% investor consent for in-specie distribution during the Liquidation Period, the unliquidated investments shall be:

answer.text: Continued to be held until liquidity emerges
Distributed mandatorily in-specie at One Rupee for performance-benchmarking purposes
Forcibly sold at any market-clearing price by SEBI
Transferred to a Cat II AIF for continued management

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 13.6.3: if the AIF fails to obtain 75% consent for in-specie distribution, the unliquidated investments are MANDATORILY distributed in-specie at ONE RUPEE (for capturing in the manager's track record and Performance Benchmarking Agency reporting). An investor unwilling to accept Re. 1 valuation must WRITE OFF the investment. **The Trap:** Option A ignores the mandatory distribution trigger. Options C, D invent powers/routes that do not exist. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C/D test the same Re. 1 mandatory-distribution rule. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Failing the 75% vote is catastrophic for the manager's Performance Benchmarking Agency record — Re. 1 valuation crushes DPI/TVPI-equivalent metrics. Spend effort chasing the vote; Re. 1 is reputational disaster even if economically trivial.
